articles.title: 国产“原子级放大镜”问世：中国科大利用拓扑探针首次实现交错磁体原子尺度自旋成像
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，中国科学技术大学科研团队将拓扑材料制成扫描隧道显微镜针尖，发展出原子尺度自旋探测新方法，并获得钾钒硒氧表面存在二维 d 波交错磁序的直接实验证据。这一针尖在未来有望成为观察电子自旋的“原子级放大镜”。该研究由中国科学技术大学物理学院陈仙辉院士、王震宇教授团队联合该校化学与材料科学学院向斌教授、香港科技大学刘军伟教授等合作者共同完成，陈仙辉、王震宇、刘军伟和向斌为共同通讯作者。相关成果于 10 月 13 日发表于刊《自然》。▲ 基于一维螺旋边界态的原子尺度自旋探测自旋是电子的基本属性，与材料的磁性密切相关。在原子尺度辨识自旋相关电子态，是研究量子材料中演生现象的重要手段。传统自旋分辨探针通常依赖针尖末端的磁性原子修饰，其自旋态可能受到针尖与样品相互作用的影响，且往往需要外磁场辅助。量子自旋霍尔体系的一维边界态具有螺旋特征：沿同一边界反向传播的电子携带相反的自旋。如果此类拓扑边界态主导量子隧穿过程，控制样品偏压的极性以改变隧穿电子的运动方向，原理上有可能获得不同的自旋选择性。此前，陈仙辉、王震宇团队在层状材料碘化铋单晶（α-Bi₄I₄）的单层和双层台阶处均观测到稳定且纯净的一维螺旋边界通道，其层间杂化耦合极弱，为利用同族拓扑材料构筑边界态针尖提供了实验思路。▲ KV2Se2O 表面二维 d 波交错磁性的实空间与动量空间实验证据研究团队通过聚焦离子束微纳加工，将 α 相溴化铋单晶制备成具有原子分辨能力的扫描隧道显微镜针尖，谱学标定证实加工后的针尖仍保留螺旋边界态的特征。为验证其自旋选择性，团队分别对铁碲中的双共线反铁磁条纹和笼目磁体铁锗中的层间反铁磁序开展测量，前者条纹对比随样品偏压极性反转，后者层间对比随磁场诱导的自旋重取向而显著变化。这些结果表明，边界态的自旋 — 动量锁定可以转化为随隧穿方向变化的自旋选择性。随后，团队将这一方法用于交错磁体候选材料钾钒硒氧的研究。交错磁体的净磁化为零，但交换作用可以在不依赖自旋 — 轨道耦合的情况下产生强的能带自旋劈裂，且自旋极化随动量方向交替变化。在钾钒硒氧表面，原子成像识别出具有√2×√2 周期的密度波调制以及两类由镜面对称联系的钒位点，对相反偏压极性的图像进行重构后获得的实空间图案与棋盘状反铁磁序相一致。矢量磁场下的隧道谱测量发现，沿两个正交晶轴延展的准粒子激发呈现相反的能量移动，支持它们具有相反的自旋极化。在准粒子干涉图样中，与 X、Y 能谷相关的两组正交散射特征具有不同强度，且其主导方向随偏压极性反转而旋转 90 度。非磁针尖及多类材料的对照实验进一步表明，实验所观察到的偏压反转行为难以被结构各向异性、局域应变或隧穿轨道选择性所解释。综合原子晶格结构、与反铁磁序一致的实空间图样、准粒子激发态的磁场响应和随偏压反转的动量空间散射各向异性，研究团队获得了相互印证的实验结果。结合理论分析和对比实验，所有结果支持了钾钒硒氧表面层的二维 d 波交错磁序。陈仙辉介绍，该工作展示了拓扑量子材料作为物态测量探针的潜力：拓扑边界态不仅可以被观测，还可以用于探测其他材料的自旋相关电子态。这一方法有望应用于二维磁体和莫尔材料，为研究其原子尺度自旋特征提供新的方法和技术。IT之家附论文链接：https://www.nature.com/articles/s41586-026-11257-1

articles.title: 育碧计划关闭芬兰 RedLynx 工作室，新加坡工作室也面临大幅裁员
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据游戏媒体 Game Industry 今天报道，育碧计划关闭芬兰 RedLynx 工作室，新加坡工作室也将面临大规模裁员，此举旨在推进重组计划、削减成本。育碧表示：“我们已经通知团队：公司拟关闭位于芬兰的 RedLynx 工作室。该计划需遵循当地协商程序，预计最多影响 52 个岗位。育碧新加坡工作室将削减 70 个岗位，使人员规模与未来项目制作相匹配。新加坡仍是育碧全球体系的重要部分，我们高度重视他们的贡献，也深知这一决定可能对同事们造成影响。我们承诺在整个过程中为团队提供支持，并以审慎、尊重的态度推进相关工作。”IT之家了解到，RedLynx 工作室于 2011 年被育碧收购，代表作品有《特技摩托 2》《特技摩托 HD》，最后一款作品为 2019 年发行的《特技摩托：聚变》，之后该工作室逐渐变为育碧支援团队。2025 年，RedLynx 曾进行过一轮裁员。当时该工作室从多平台游戏开发商转型为“专注于小屏游戏”，开发两款未公布的手游。据了解，RedLynx 目前尚未被分配到任何项目，也没有能够独立持续运营的游戏作品。

articles.title: 宝马 7 系重返 V8 动力时代，2027 款 M760 xDrive 搭载 4.4T V8 发动机、570 马力
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，宝马在今年 4 月发布 G70 世代 7 系中期改款车型时，产品线中并没有八缸选项，当时宝马方面表示 V8 M Performance 车型会在 2027 年跟进。据 Car and Driver 报道，2027 款宝马 M760 xDrive 已正式亮相，搭载一台 4.4 升双涡轮增压 V8 发动机，最大功率约 570 马力，标配 xDrive 全轮驱动，底盘部件相较直列六缸的 740 车型有所升级。新车计划于 2027 年上半年登陆美国市场，起售价预计超过 12.6 万美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 84.5 万元人民币），宝马尚未公布完整性能参数和最终定价。此次推出的 M760 xDrive 与此前的 760i xDrive 在动力配置上有所不同。上一代 G12 车型搭载 6.6 升双涡轮增压 V12 发动机，最大功率为 601 马力，峰值扭矩约 800 牛 · 米。新款车型改用 4.4 升双涡轮增压 V8 发动机，车型名称也从 M760i 调整为 M760，因为“i”后缀今后将专用于宝马的纯电车型。据 BMW Blog 报道，新款 M760 xDrive 的推出旨在填补改款 7 系此前缺少 V8 动力车型的空缺。与上一代 760i xDrive 不同，新车还将进入欧洲市场销售。据 Motor1 报道，7 系由此形成三款 M Performance 车型分别对应三种动力形式的格局，而 M760 xDrive 取代的是此前 760i 的位置，功率比 760i 的 536 马力高出约 34 马力。M760 xDrive 将纳入宝马 M Performance 高性能产品序列，与插电式混合动力车型 M760e xDrive、纯电动车型 i7 M70 xDrive 并列。这意味着，7 系将分别通过燃油 V8、插电式混合动力和纯电动三种动力形式提供 M Performance 车型。外观方面，新车采用 M Sport Pro 套件对应的前脸设计，配备 22 英寸轮毂、带有 M 条纹的后视镜外壳以及 M760 专属标识。车尾部分，新车保留了外露式排气管，并采用运动风格更鲜明的扩散器设计，与普通版 7 系形成区别。内饰方面，新车配备带 12 点钟位置标记的 M Sport 方向盘，并加入专属氛围灯以及 iDrive X 系统中的宝马 M 相关内容。这些设计主要目的在于让 V8 车型在视觉上与 740 等普通版本形成区分。值得关注的是，M760 并非这一代 7 系唯一的 V8 车型。据 BMW Blog 报道，宝马 ALPINA 已确认其新时代首款 V8 车型将基于改款 7 系打造，内部代号 G72，定位高于普通宝马 7 系但低于劳斯莱斯古思特。与 M760 追求峰值功率不同，ALPINA 版本预计将侧重低扭输出和长途巡航的平顺性，动力系统可能采用轻混辅助而非插电混动方案。

articles.title: 现代汽车印度新工厂投产：总年产能接近 100 万辆，计划 2032 年前对印度投资 155 亿美元
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据韩国先驱报报道，现代汽车印度浦那工厂今日正式投产，初始年产能为 17 万辆，计划到 2030 年提升至 32 万辆。随着新工厂落成，现代汽车目前在印度共运营三家生产厂，总年产能接近 100 万辆。依托该工厂规划的 32 万辆年产能，现代汽车印度公司计划在 2030 年前将出口占其总产量的比重提升至 30%。此外，现代汽车集团会长郑义宣 13 日在印度新德里拜会印度总理纳伦德拉 · 莫迪，商讨对印度汽车产业的投资计划。现代汽车计划在 2032 年前投资 155 亿美元（IT之家注：现汇率约合 1,039.28 亿元人民币）增设印度汽车生产设施并建立研发设施，并在当地构建包括未来技术创新的综合性汽车产业生态。为切实有效执行上述大规模投资计划，现代汽车将在印度设立专门投资法人。现代汽车表示，目前公司在印度境内雇佣员工数量达 2.4 万多人，期待这次投资推动制造、研发、工程、供应链等领域工作岗位进一步增加。截至今年第三季度，现代汽车在印度累计销量达到 988.496 万辆。现代汽车和起亚所属的现代汽车集团去年在印度汽车市场占有率突破 19%。

articles.title: AI 挖掘的漏洞报告存在误报，华为终端安全奖励计划要求提交前进行人工分析和验证
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，华为安全应急响应中心今日发布华为终端安全奖励计划关于后续漏洞报告处置规则的公告。官方表示，今年收到了大量利用 AI 工具辅助挖掘的漏洞报告，其中大多数报告都提供了 PoC（IT之家注：概念验证，证明某个安全漏洞确实存在且可被触发的代码、脚本、请求数据包或详细复现步骤），但仍不可避免地存在因 AI“幻觉”误导而产生的误报。为了合理分配有限的审核资源，确保华为终端安全奖励计划审核团队能聚焦于真实有效的漏洞，同时维护健康有序的社区生态，现提出如下要求：一、漏洞报告要求对于 AI 辅助或自动化发现的漏洞报告，提交前务必进行人工分析和验证。我们鼓励白帽子提供完整的 EXP 攻击链验证，请确保报告中提供漏洞实际安全影响的证明，包括但不限于：动态可执行的完整 PoC；受影响的产品、系统版本和危害说明（注：要求漏洞影响产品须在奖励计划范围内且已升级至最新 HarmonyOS 系统版本）；报告内容清晰易懂，复现步骤简洁明了；完整日志及结果截图 / 演示视频；攻击路径必须从实际攻击场景的入口触发并且证明产生实际的安全影响。二、不规范行为白帽子在参与奖励计划的全过程中，应始终保持相互尊重，以专业、友好的方式和语气交流。禁止以下行为：持续、重复、大量提交由 AI 直接生成、未经人工复现、未通过最新可调用接口触发、截取不完整代码片段分析验证或未提供可证明实际安全影响的验证结果的无效报告；歪曲事实、恶意抹黑华为终端安全奖励计划或实施言语攻击、辱骂、威胁、骚扰工作人员及刷屏留言等恶意行为。三、不规范行为处置对于上述第 1 项行为，平台将直接驳回相关报告，且不逐一说明驳回原因。对于累计提交 3 份上述无效报告的账号，平台将予以提醒；累计达到 5 份的，平台有权封禁其华为安全奖励计划账号。对于上述第 2 项行为，华为终端安全奖励计划有权立即终止其账号持有人（含团队 / 组织）的参与资格或对其实施永久封禁。此外，官方还调整了工具类漏洞受理范围：自 2026 年 9 月 30 日起，暂不受理华为终端工具（如 DevEco 等）的漏洞。但若您发现了可导致自研工具公有仓供应链投毒类漏洞或利用该工具可影响华为终端设备安全的漏洞，仍可提交，我们将根据漏洞影响等因素综合评估后予以答复。

articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，小米汽车今日宣布，正式启动「北方八省冬季服务关怀」专项行动，多项免费服务与保障政策同步上线。IT之家附服务内容如下：活动信息活动时间：2026 年 10 月 15 日至 2027 年 3 月 31 日适用地区：包括黑龙江、吉林、辽宁、内蒙古、新疆、青海、甘肃、宁夏六大专属关怀免费冬季专项检查（限 1 次）：冬季用车，安全先行。活动期间，每车可到店享受一次免费冬季专项检查，包括全车灯光、底盘悬架、轮胎胎压 / 胎纹、制动盘与制动片状态、雨刮功能、蓄电池状态等 15 项车辆安全健康检查。根据车辆情况免费加注防冻玻璃清洗液和防冻液，让爱车从容应对严寒。免费借用轮胎防滑链（按需）：积雪路面行驶，防滑链是重要保障。活动期间，车主可按需免费借用轮胎防滑链，借用需提前 3 天通过小米汽车 App 进行预约，签署借用协议后按指引正确安装使用。防滑链仅限积雪或结冰路面使用，行驶速度不超过 50 公里每小时，进入无雪路段需及时拆除。具体适配规格与安装方式，可咨询服务中心工作人员。更换冬季胎免工时费（免费更换、还原各 1 次）：活动期间，每辆车可享受免费更换并还原全车冬季轮胎各一次，用户需自带轮胎，拆装与四轮动平衡工时费全免，冬季胎与常规胎切换更省心。免费轮胎存储服务：换下的轮胎没处放？小米汽车提供免费冬季轮胎存储服务，可寄存至 2027 年 12 月 31 日。您签署轮胎存储协议后门店将为每条轮胎张贴专属标识妥善保管。服务范围为指定服务中心，单店限前 100 名，先到先得，建议提前通过小米汽车官方热线或小米汽车 APP 专属服务群进行预约。免费道路救援（事故、亏电救援无忧）：冬季路况复杂，如遇故障或事故导致车辆无法正常行驶、或继续行驶存在较大风险，小米汽车免费提供道路救援，跨城、无距离、无次数限制。轮胎扎钉、车辆亏电无法行驶等情况，就近拖车至门店或充电站。免费异地维修送还：如车辆需送往活动地区内服务中心进行维修，维修完毕后，小米汽车服务中心提供异地免费送车服务，修车不用自己奔波，省事、省心。

articles.title: 长城汽车：传感器装得多，辅助驾驶系统不一定就好用，关键是要看得准
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，长城汽车官方微博今日发文，谈及了汽车辅助驾驶系统。长城官方表示，传感器装得多，辅助驾驶系统不一定就好用，关键是要看得准。据长城汽车介绍，其智能辅助驾驶传感器验证试验室，硬件安装精度 2mm 以内，数百次压测把误差锁定在 0.3° 以内，让“眼睛”看得更准。据IT之家此前报道，长城汽车魏牌 CEO 赵永坡在今年 3 月也发布视频表达过类似观点。他认为，特斯拉笃信纯视觉，国内多数车企选择激光雷达 + 视觉融合。但传感器越多未必越好，内耗反而抵消优势。赵永坡视频用气球举例，当搭载激光雷达 + 视觉融合方案的车辆在行驶过程中遇到了一个气球时，激光雷达会扫描并告诉汽车前方有球状物体，但材质不知；摄像头会捕捉到气球的画面，并通过算法告诉汽车前方是一个软的气球。但汽车的算力和路径规划处于一种内耗之中，背离了使用两种传感器方案优势去叠加出好选择的初衷。

articles.title: 日立推出木制数据中心，主打低成本、亲和外观
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，日立制作所今日宣布推出木制数据中心，该产品是公司旗下小型数据中心“Flexible Design Container”的新型号，具备低成本、建设周期短等优点。由于立柱等部分采用木材，它不仅能够更好融入城市环境，还能吸收二氧化碳。据官方介绍，该产品采用模块化设计，可降低部署成本和周期，提升 IT 设备的运行效率。日立对此表示：“与建筑物式数据中心相比，该产品可安装在工厂空地等场所，不需要配备大规模电源。”IT之家了解到，该产品在立柱、横梁等主要承重结构中使用木材。与钢筋混凝土相比，木材重量更轻、易于处理，适合采用预制装配式施工工艺，可以提升施工效率。根据日立制作所估算，该产品可实现 20 吨二氧化碳减排效果。此外，这款数据中心的外墙同样使用木材，配合场地绿化等措施，可打造与城市景观协调的效果。日立制作所表示：“即使在靠近居民生活区的地点，也能够建设兼顾周边环境和当地特色的数据中心，从而推动与当地社区达成共识，提高社会接受度。”安全方面，该数据中心满足建筑坚固性要求，达到抗震安全标准最高等级“I 类”。即使发生大地震，建筑物也可在无需修复的情况下继续使用，寿命超 30 年。该产品支持气体灭火系统、防入侵措施，以及电子门锁、摄像头的出入管理系统。相关阅读：《Meta 加入微软行列：试点将重型木结构引入数据中心建造》《微软旗下首个“木材打造”数据中心在美国弗吉尼亚州开建，号称可减少 35% 碳排放量》

articles.title: SK 海力士预测：到 2030 年，AI 基础设施性能规模将增长约 20 倍
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，据韩联社报道，SK 海力士开发总管安炫（Ahn Hyun）今日在首尔江南区 COEX 举行的“第 28 届韩国半导体大展”(SEDEX 2026) 上发表主旨演讲。他预测称，2030 年 AI 基础设施性能规模将增长约 20 倍。安炫指出，当前 AI 推理市场正同时在三个维度快速扩张：任务复杂度的提升、单次处理信息量（上下文长度）的激增，以及推理请求量的井喷。这些因素相互交织，推动了 AI 算力基础设施需求的迅猛增长。随着 AI 推理需求的暴增，承担海量数据存储与迁移任务的存储器，其关键地位愈发凸显。特别是用于保存并复用前序处理信息的“键值缓存（KV Cache）”容量持续膨胀，迫使系统必须将数据分摊存储于高带宽内存 HBM、DRAM 以及 SSD 等不同介质中。分析表明，在此过程中产生的数据迁移，正演变为制约性能提升并推高系统能耗的全新瓶颈。对此，安炫作出了这一预测，即人工智能基础设施的性能规模到 2030 年将增长约 20 倍。安炫强调，行业不能仅停留在提升单一存储芯片的性能上，而亟需采取优化整个存储层次结构的全局方案。为此，SK 海力士在持续优化现有 HBM 性能的同时，正全力推进 3D 堆叠 DRAM 以及高带宽闪存 HBF 等下一代存储技术的研发：3D 堆叠 DRAM：通过在 GPU、NPU 等逻辑芯片之上直接堆叠 DRAM，在大幅跃升传输性能的同时显著降低能耗。高带宽闪存 HBF：将成熟应用于 HBM 的硅通孔立体堆叠与高速 I/O 接口技术导入 NAND 闪存，旨在 HBM 与 DRAM 之间开辟全新的存储层级。IT之家从报道获悉，SK 海力士的目标是将 HBF 的带宽做到同代 HBM 的 50% 左右，同时实现约 10 倍的容量扩容。

articles.title: 华为详解鸿蒙座舱「智慧场景」：一套条件 + 动作的车载自动化规则，支持触发后执行系列操作
articles.content: IT之家 10 月 14 日消息，华为智能汽车解决方案 BU 官方微博今日发布乾崑答网友问（第 17 期），针对鸿蒙座舱的「智慧场景」是什么、基于 MoLA 2.0 架构的小艺智能体有哪些功能等问题进行了集中解答。IT之家附本期华为乾崑答网友问重点内容如下：鸿蒙座舱的「智慧场景」是什么？鸿蒙座舱智慧场景，是一套条件 + 动作的车载自动化规则。设定好触发条件后，车辆会自动执行一系列操作，不用手动一步步点控、下发指令。触发条件：主驾入座、挂入 D 挡、到达设定时间、副驾入座等车载场景。执行动作：条件满足后，自动执行多项操作，比如播报日程、启动导航、调节空调、播放专属音乐、开启座椅功能等。典型实用场景：下班放松场景：上车挂入 D 挡（触发条件），系统自动播放舒缓音乐，同时启动回家导航（执行动作），一键解锁轻松通勤体验。仪式感惊喜场景：副驾入座并系好安全带（触发条件），自动开启座椅按摩、播报生日祝福、播放生日歌曲（执行动作），打造专属用车仪式感。基于 MoLA 2.0 架构的小艺智能体有哪些常用功能？基于 MoLA 2.0 架构的小艺智能体，涵盖导航、人车交互、影音、畅聊、KFC 点餐等多款实用智能体，下面介绍两大核心智能体：导航智能体：超模糊地址导航1. 超模糊地址搜索：仅凭场景特征、相对位置、出行目的等口语化描述，即可精准定位目的地。示例：语音“导航到广州珠江新城能拍到小蛮腰的那个广场”，识别到花城广场；出“前往那座有生蚝壳墙面的古村落”，精准找到大岭村。2. 多途经点智能规划：支持一次性添加多个途经点，沿途查找景点、商铺，结合实时路况动态调整路线，自动规划最优行程。示例：语音“从广州出发，先去大岭村，中途找一家粤式茶餐厅吃饭，最后到花城广场”，自动串联全部点位，规划顺路高效路线。人车交互智能体：听得懂，控得准人车交互智能体可精准识别用户深层用车意图，不再局限固定死板指令，轻松理解生活化口语。1. 场景意图识别：说出“玻璃起雾了”，自动开启前挡风玻璃除霜；说“车里有点热”，自动调低空调温度。2. 生活化口语交互：识别日常通俗说法，像“收起车耳朵”折叠后视镜，“打开车耳朵加热”开启后视镜加热，人车交互更自然丝滑。

articles.title: AI 短剧日产 1500 部：一场全员狂飙下的 「无人生还」
articles.content: “现在整个短剧行业就是一片混乱，每个人都很焦虑、很迷茫。”这是过去一个月里，雷峰网与多位 AI 短剧从业者交流时，听到最多的一句话。上个月刚跑通的流程，这个月平台改了分账规则又得重新算账。好不容易摸清了提示词的写法，AI 视频生成工具一更新经验立马作废。甲方的尾款还没到账，下一部剧的制作成本已经垫出去了。这个行业节奏快到近乎疯狂，但没人说得清终点和方向。眼下，AI 短剧日上线量已突破 1500 部，制作成本从真人剧的几十上百万压缩到五万以内，大批团队仍在涌入赛道。可几乎所有受访者传递同一个信号：除了平台，几乎没人真正赚到钱。01 一部剧的生死，只有三天用传统内容生意的逻辑很难理解 AI 短剧，它更像一场高速运转的概率赌局。今年 8 月底，短剧编剧朱晓冉选择从大厂辞职。在真人短剧时代，编剧花一个月打磨本子是常态，但AI 短剧爆发后，她的工作节奏被彻底改写。“领导觉得有了 AI 工具，写本效率也该跟着上来。上半年最忙的时候，我一个月交了四个本子。剧本送交承制方后，几天就能产出成片。”产量快速拉高，质量却很快摸到了天花板。在朱晓冉看来，纯人工打磨的剧本可以做到九十分甚至一百分，AI 辅助创作的剧本上限大多只有八十分。“老板也很清楚这一点，但他更想要四个八十分，而不是一个一百分。” 朱晓冉表示。“这个行业现在本质是靠量赌概率，我们统计过 AI 短剧的爆率大概是千分之四，其余的基本都是无效产出。” 朱晓冉解释了一下这个逻辑，就算前面花六百万拍十部都扑了，只要第十一部赚了七百万覆盖全部亏损，这套商业模式就成立。“真人短剧粗制滥造一点三四十万就能拍出来，精品剧的制作费得一百万到一百五十万左右，但现在一部AI短剧的总投入五万就能搞定。”分成上，朱晓冉透露通常是编剧几千到一万，制作两三万到三四万，整个环节的总成本被压得极低。但产出剧集只是开始，拿到曝光才是整个环节的生死关口。“一部剧上线后，三天内没起量基本就凉了，不会有什么长尾效应。因为曝光最集中的时间就是前三天投流期，如果三天内起不来，大家就会立马放弃投流转投新剧。” 朱晓冉坦言。拥有九年影视从业经验的短剧导演瑾诺分享，短剧极度依赖投流，纯靠自然流量做火的案例业内确实也有，但概率几乎等于中大乐透。“投流这个环节大平台有专门的运营部门和投流手，外面也有专门的投流公司，好的投流手甚至能把一个一般的剧本投成大爆款。”但就算有投流加持，AI 短剧也会遭遇流量瓶颈。“某短剧平台的流量池有个别称叫‘流量黑盒子’，热度到 4000 万推你去下一层，5000 万再推。但 AI 漫剧到 4000 万就上不去了，开始卡流量。当然，推流机制没人知道，内部是否可以操控，无人知晓。” 瑾诺说。流量之外，收入也越来越少。目前在多数平台模式下，制作方收入主要分为两块：平台给剧本的保底金，以及剧集上线后的播放量分成。瑾诺坦言，“上半年国内 AI 短剧市场还能赚钱的，但现在不行了。因为很多短剧平台调整了分成规则，现在做 AI 漫剧可能横屏能小赚一点，但是整体要求也会相对应更高，不然自制基本亏本。”规则确实在变，今年4 月，红果率先下调AI 漫剧基础分账系数：AI 仿真人分账系数从 60 下调至 40，3D 漫剧从 50 下调至 40，同时取消中小团队 AI 仿真人剧本普惠保底。到了9月，红果又在《优质 AI 剧生产活动 2.0》中，取消了行业批量做 IP 续集赖以获利的系列剧规模系数。对靠批量做 IP 续集获利的团队来说，这条路也收窄了。“能拿到可观分成的只有金字塔尖极少数，大部分项目连成本都收不回来。” 朱晓冉补充。02 月薪三千的抽卡师，一周见真招的 AI 导演外界普遍认为AI降低了短剧行业的准入门槛，但在一线从业者视角，这反而是对从业者能力的重新洗牌。AI 介入生产短剧生产之后，催生了一个新岗位 —— 抽卡师。编剧只负责完成剧本，但AI视频生成工具读不懂剧本，需要有人把每一个镜头拆解成工具能理解的提示词描述，这就是抽卡师的工作。朱晓冉举了一个例子，“比如剧本写‘他看着对方’，抽卡师就要扩写成带表情、神态的详细描述，然后把这段描述喂给 AI 反复生成画面，直到抽出一个合格的镜头，视频生成环节真正做视觉细化的是抽卡师。”这是链条里不可或缺的一环，虽然用人量很大，但在行业内却属于"黑工"。“老板觉得没什么技术含量，就是把人话翻译给 AI 听，所以工资压得很低，但 KPI 又压得很重。这个岗位非常重要，但在现有模式下更像是很苦的纯力工。”朱晓冉表示。都是抽卡，但同一套AI生成工具，不同的人交出的结果完全天差地别。瑾诺认为，AI 就像一个加速器，把从业者的天赋、能力差距极度放大。“因为 AI 的考核更透明，有经验的人一个镜头两三次就能出，返工率高的人要七八次，这个成本差就会达到一倍以上。达

articles.content: 香港，2026年10月13日——全球领先的AI视频大模型公司爱诗科技（AIsphere）今日宣布其香港办公室在香港数码港正式开幕。其香港办公室不仅是办公空间，更定位为辐射本地企业、政府机构、高校及创作者的AI枢纽。开幕当日香港办公室即投入运营，公司日后将招募更多本地员工并持续举办面向产业的专场活动，逐步建设汇聚创作者、高校与产业伙伴的「香港AI视频大本营」。爱诗科技联合创始人兼总裁谢旭璋及署理投资推广署署长刘智元、香港数码港行政总裁郑松岩博士、香港引进重点企业办公室副总监杨树源、香港生产力促进局主管等重要嘉宾出席剪彩仪式，与在港科技企业、金融投资机构、高校及社会各界代表共同见证爱诗科技落地香港。首度公布本地合作，启动「数智香港·爱诗AI百业共创计划」香港特区政府近日公布《施政报告》及首份五年规划（2026—2030年），明确提出以人工智能赋能千行百业、持续推进「人工智能+」行动，并加快算力基础设施建设、提升市民人工智能素养，为本地AI产业发展提供清晰指引。在此背景下，作为首批正式在港设立办公室的AI视频大模型公司，爱诗科技在开幕当日即宣布开启「数智香港·爱诗AI百业共创计划」，向香港各界发出合作邀请。谢旭璋在接受媒体采访时表示：「香港拥有国际化的视野、扎实的科研基础和活跃的创意产业，是我们全球发展的重要一站。作为港投公司科技生态圈的企业，我们希望成为连接香港各行业的AI枢纽。未来，我们将和香港本地高校共同举办AI视频模型相关的学术论坛，更希望与本地企业、青年与创作者一起，把AI视频和实时世界模型的能力真正用到产业和创作中去。」开幕当日，爱诗科技与在港科技企业、高等院校及青年社会团体签署多项战略合作文件，共同推动香港AI应用的落地与发展。在产业合作方面，公司与空间智能企业其域创新达成战略合作，融合真实世界三维重建与AI视频生成技术，围绕影视、文旅、地产等行业场景探索联合解决方案，携手开拓海外市场；在教育科研方面，公司与香港理工大学开展合作，将AI视频创作引入人文教学，结合中国历史与文化课程，探索负责任AI与数字叙事的教学实践，并在此基础上拓展人才培养、学生实习及联合研究等合作方向，推动产学研协同发展。此外，爱诗科技亦非常重视AI视频模型在社会服务方面的实际应用，推动技术真正走向普惠。公司当日宣布与香港福建三明联会青年委员会携手，未来将面向在港乡亲及青年开展AI科普讲座、创作体验工作坊及科技企业参访，并依托其闽港两地网络，联合开展「AI看三明」等两地青年交流与AI文化共创活动；同时，公司也与本地社团香港青年新创见展开合作，探索AI技术在社团建设、社区服务及青年交流中的应用，如在社区和学校开展AI讲座、运用AI视频制作防诈骗等公益内容，以及支持「一带一路」沿线青年交流活动。「系统化的科普展示和互动体验可提升大众对AI的理性认知，为技术应用营造更加包容、稳健的社会环境，夯实人工智能在香港长期发展的社会基础。」爱诗科技香港首席代表潘援介绍。PixVerse articles.title: ChunkAct: Action Chunking for Agentic Robotics
articles.content: Agentic robotics places a large language model (LLM) agent in the robot control loop, where it composes perception, motion, and vision-language-action (VLA) tools under the guidance of a memory and thereby generalizes to new tasks without retraining. This generality comes at a steep price in efficiency. Every primitive requires a round of LLM reasoning over the full interaction history, so the cost of an episode grows with the number of primitives. We find this reasoning largely redundant: once a sub-goal is chosen, its primitives follow a routine already prescribed by memory. We present ChunkAct, which introduces action chunking to agentic robotics. Online, a single call launches a chunk of chained primitives, which executes autonomously and returns control only upon failure. Offline, ChunkAct compiles the memory into these chunks, so execution is memory-free at test time and the planner is reserved for decisions that require reasoning. LLM computation therefore scales with the number of decisions rather than the number of primitives. On LIBERO-Pro, ChunkAct improves task success by 5.0 points over the state of the art in agentic robotics while requiring 2.9x fewer LLM calls, 4.4x fewer input tokens, and 2.3x fewer output tokens.

articles.title: LoopWAM: Closed-Loop Generalist Policy Improvement from Deployment Rollouts
articles.content: Scaling expert demonstrations alone does not enable generalist robot policies to improve from deployment. Real-world rollouts contain successes, suboptimal behavior, and failures: imitating every recorded action can reinforce poor behavior, while filtering out failures discards evidence of physical interactions and their consequences. We introduce \textbf{LoopWAM}, a closed-loop world-action model that learns directly from this full quality spectrum, using rollouts from both itself and other deployed policies. Source-dependent noise sampling unifies behavior learning and action-conditioned world modeling, while quality steering and quality-weighted supervision retain full video supervision across qualities and regulate action imitation. Video and action tokens interact throughout parallel denoising, allowing learned consequences to inform action generation directly. On RoboChallenge Table30-V2, three deployment-and-training rounds raise success from 23.67\% to 43.33\%, a 19.7-percentage-point gain, with a final score of 56.80. LoopWAM also achieves 94.5\% average success on RoboTwin~2.0 and 49.5\% overall success on RoboCasa365 without additional embodied pretraining, obtaining the best overall results among the compared methods across all three benchmarks. On challenging shirt folding task, two rounds of deployment-driven improvement after single-task post-training raise success from 13.20\% to 55.56\%. These results demonstrate closed-loop improvement from mixed-quality experience under both multi-task learning and single-task post-training. \href{https://loop-wam.github.io/}{\textcolor{orange}{Project Page}}

articles.title: EgoExplorer: A Vision-Motion-Touch Observatory for Human Loco-Manipulation In Situ
articles.content: Learning humanoid loco-manipulation from human demonstrations rests on observing how locomotion, posture, and object interaction evolve together as tasks unfold. Scaling collection across diverse environments, in turn, favors lightweight, portable capture systems. Yet, existing datasets provide only partial views of this coordination. Thus, we introduce EgoExplorer, a 100-hour vision-motion-touch observatory of human loco-manipulation built with a wearable system. With an emphasis on professional activities, its continuous recordings align egocentric video with reconstructed whole-body motion, fine-grained finger articulation, and tactile observations, accompanied by step-level descriptions. To achieve this coverage with sparse body sensing, we develop the Calibrate-Complete-Constrain pipeline. Concretely, reusable calibration fixes participant geometry and sensor attachments before motion inference to disentangle mounting offsets from articulation. A temporal prior then completes unobserved joint motion, while layered constraints promote measurement agreement, temporal continuity, and geometric consistency, properties that motion plausibility alone does not guarantee. Against tracker-fitted references, the method reduces body-point error by 71.9% relative to the strongest baseline; matched evaluations also show gains in hand stability and contact estimation. Preliminary studies explore multimodal generation and conditioning alongside humanoid retargeting with whole-body control in simulation.

articles.title: Dog-Breed Text-to-image Flow Matching from Pretraining to Fine-Tuning on 4 Consumer GPUs
articles.content: We generally perceive that training text-to-image diffusion models requires heavy compute: it is true if we aim at a comprehensive frontier model. This understanding prevents people from training their own models when getting started in the field. We develop MiniDog, a framework that enables pretraining diffusion transformers in 55 minutes and fine-tuning in another 15 minutes on four 3090 GPUs. For data, we use 26k dog images from ImageNet and caption them for pretraining and use 2k images generated by FLUX.1-schnell for fine-tuning. We precompute the image and text features and cache them for efficiency. For architecture, we use E2E-INVAE for its semantic latent space, a small transformer with 22M parameters, a small Qwen model for text encoding, and in-context conditioning. For training, we use iREPA and an EUPE perception encoder for acceleration. For evaluation, our repository supports FID, HPSv2 score, PickScore, and various VAE reconstruction metrics.

articles.title: Cepheid: Decoupling Scale from Structure for Cross-Family Motion Completion
articles.content: Sparse-to-dense motion completion recovers dense mesh motion from sparse vertex displacements. Residual priors trained on one geometry family frequently fail to beat parameter-free harmonic extension off-family. Moreover, cross-family training meets a scaling barrier: residual amplitude varies by more than an order of magnitude across geometry families and collapses as observations become denser. Since this scale depends on unknown target motion, it cannot be measured directly at test time. We decouple residual structure from physical scale by learning a dimensionless prior, estimating amplitude from observables and a lightweight correction fitted only on training sources. Our unified model surpasses harmonic extension across all evaluated families, including unseen cloth and legged bodies, without skeletons, registration, or cross-mesh correspondence. The same prior applies without retraining to point-tracked animal video and a robot grasping a soft body. Project page: https://su-terry.github.io/cepheid-website/

articles.content: How should demonstration quality be used during vision-language-action (VLA) pretraining to improve performance after target-task fine-tuning? We compare weighting, filtering, and conditioning across reward definitions and label granularities using 5,000 naturally suboptimal human demonstrations and 24 target tasks. Within each VLA, we match demonstrations and training budgets. Additional comparisons examine pretraining data size and the roles of quality tags during fine-tuning and inference. Across three VLAs, we find that approach-aware episode conditioning improves mean success over plain behavioral cloning; conditioning and filtering favor episode and chunk labels, respectively, on average, with model-dependent reversals; and constant-tag fine-tuning improves mean success after conditioned pretraining with either tagged or untagged inference. We introduce AXIS-Bench to support these controlled comparisons. Built on crowdsourced simulation demonstrations, it provides recorded object and contact states for recomputing quality labels on shared trajectories. Replayable trajectories support workspace-aligned rendering and user-defined real-world target tasks. In our real-world experiment, simulation pretraining raises success from 9.6\% to 31.7\%. articles.title: Tev: Scaling Long-Horizon Agentic Environments with Dense Progress Rewards
articles.content: Long-horizon agents have drawn growing attention for their ability to work autonomously -- from hours to days -- on economically valuable tasks, a capability essential to automated discovery and recursive self-improvement (RSI). Yet open-source models still struggle on long-horizon tasks, largely for lack of both training data and a working recipe, and scaling both is hard: long, complex tasks are difficult to curate and verify, and their rewards are sparse. We address both. First, we introduce Tev-Gym, the first long-horizon agent training dataset with verifiable, dense, progressive rewards -- 1,170 verified task environments across 7 domains. It is built on a latent-world-first approach that first constructs a latent world: a complete and correct hidden specification of the task domain, workflow, and expected state after each step. Each task is then progressively rendered from this specification into an agent-facing environment, enabling controllable complexity and a natural progress metric. Second, we turn this metric into a training recipe: via progress-potential reward shaping (PPRS), we convert progress into a dense per-step reward that improves training efficiency and makes otherwise-intractable tasks trainable. Training with this recipe yields Tev-27B, which achieves substantial gains on the Agents' Last Exam computing and math sciences domains (ALE-CM), matching GPT-6 Astra and Claude Opus 5 at Pass@5. Despite training only on ALE-related data, it generalizes to the Terminal-Bench (TB) 3.0 and 4.0 subsets, surpassing GLM 5.2 and Gemini 3.7 Flash, and reaches Claude Opus 4.8-level performance on middle-horizon tasks such as TB 2.1.

articles.title: EmbodiedEvo: Self-improving Coding Agents for Physical Intelligence
articles.content: Bringing general-purpose agents into the physical world calls for an executable representation of physical intelligence. Compared with vision-language-action (VLA) models, which map observations and language instructions directly to actions, code makes control logic explicit and reusable. Code can serve not only as a policy representation but also as the workspace in which the agent solves a task. Rather than following a prescribed workflow of planning, execution, and verification, the agent can autonomously inspect the state, revise and execute code, and use feedback to choose the next step. The success of this SWE-style loop in digital environments motivates its extension to physical tasks. Yet physical execution remains prone to recurring failures. To retain and refine experience for later scenes, we introduce EmbodiedEvo, where a coding agent evolves reusable Skills and Lessons through feedback on a single Playground scene, then freezes the resulting harness for diverse new scenes. On RoboDojo-Sim, EmbodiedEvo achieves an average score of 44.48 and a success rate of 37.82\%, surpassing all officially verified results. Paired tests show the largest gains on memory-dependent tasks and successful reuse of coordinated procedures, while fine contact control remains difficult. Experience from stronger models also improves weaker executors: Astra's experience raises Sol and Luna's success rates by 8.86 and 5.50 percentage points over no experience. Compared with raw interaction history, Skills and Lessons achieve comparable task performance at 53.0\% lower execution cost.

articles.title: PLAYGROUND: Progressive Layout Generation with Render-Grounded Planning
articles.content: Generating editable graphic designs requires arranging visual and textual elements into a coherent composition while preserving their content and editability. Although recent MLLM-based approaches employ iterative generation and visual refinement to reflect the real-world design workflows, their high-level plans are predetermined prior to execution, limiting their adaptability as the design evolves. To address this limitation, we propose PlayGround, a progressive layout generation framework that dynamically adapts to the current rendered canvas. PlayGround establishes a progressive design loop comprising a Progressive Planner, a Layout Generator, and a Visual Verifier, guided by a Structure-Aware Retriever. Given an initial set of unordered elements, the Structure-Aware Retriever initially infers a coarse layout structure to retrieve structurally similar reference designs. Subsequently, at each turn, the Progressive Planner examines the current rendered canvas alongside the remaining elements, forms the next functional group, and plans its composition. The Layout Generator then predicts editable layout attributes, while the Visual Verifier evaluates rendered candidates and provides feedback when refinement is necessary. To train the Progressive Planner with step-wise supervision, we construct a two-stage data generation pipeline that extracts functional groups and turn-level planning trajectories from completed designs. Experiments on Crello and LICA demonstrate the effectiveness of PlayGround over existing methods. Our code and weights will be publicly released.

articles.title: AutoAgent0: An Agentic Runtime for Safe Closed-Loop Driving
articles.content: Safe autonomous driving requires more than accurate planning at a single frame: it demands reliable closed-loop execution in dynamic environments. Although end-to-end driving policies have advanced rapidly, the accumulated closed-loop errors, especially in unseen scenarios, can push vehicles into states from which the same policy struggles to recover. We address the challenge by treating closed-loop driving safety as a test-time execution problem. We introduce AutoAgent0, an agentic runtime and harness framework that augments existing driving experts with complementary detection skills, rule-based action verification, and feedback-driven recovery. To address inaccurate scene perception, an independent detection module constructs scene context using complementary perception skills, and a rule-based verifier checks proposed trajectories against this context before execution. When the nominal trajectories are unreliable, the orchestrator of the runtime activates Recovery Planning, where an agentic loop constructs alternative action proposals from action primitives and iteratively refines them using verification feedback. This design combines independent scene assessment with feasibility checks and online recovery, addressing both perception errors and the limited recovery capabilities of individual experts. Evaluations on Fail2Drive and NavSafe-$\infty$ demonstrate improved closed-loop robustness over single-expert execution in long-tail and safety-critical scenarios. These results demonstrate that runtime supervision can improve closed-loop robustness across multiple driving experts without retraining the underlying policies.

articles.title: Data Free Training of Diffusion Models for Lattice Field Theories
articles.content: Sampling equilibrium field configurations remains a major computational bottleneck in lattice field theory, motivating the development of generative samplers that can produce independent configurations. Diffusion models are promising for this purpose, but their standard denoising score matching objective requires samples from the target distribution, seemingly reintroducing the original sampling problem. Here, we show that diffusion models can instead be trained from their own generated samples using the target score identity, provided access to the unnormalized probability density. Importance-weighted formulations of this identity yield a consistent target throughout training, while unweighted variants define a self-consistent fixed-point training scheme. We benchmark the different approaches in two-dimensional \(φ^4\) theory and identify effective choices that enable efficient training and sampling across the symmetric, critical, and broken phases. Ultimately, our data-free training approach achieves comparable performance to training on HMC reference data.

articles.title: DoubtLess: Training-Free Contrastive Decoding for Efficient Reasoning
articles.content: Reasoning models achieve strong performance through long chains of thought (CoT), but often spend more tokens than needed to solve a problem. Existing ways to shorten the CoT require additional training for each model, add a fixed steering vector to the model's hidden states, or use decoding heuristics such as stopping early or banning words like "wait", which can reduce accuracy. We propose DoubtLess, a training-free decoding method in which a much smaller reasoning model steers the large one towards brevity. The small model reads the large model's CoT so far twice, once prompted to be brief (the brief thinker) and once prompted to be verbose (the verbose thinker), and the difference between its two logit vectors, scaled by a strength, is added to the large model's logits at every step of the CoT. On seven benchmarks of competition mathematics, graduate-level science and competitive programming, DoubtLess shortens the CoT of Qwen3-32B by 31% with unchanged accuracy, outperforming five inference-time baselines. We also show that DoubtLess reduces thinking tokens per turn by 20% in a self-debugging coding agent with unchanged task performance. It also generalizes to two other model families with unchanged accuracy. When combined with training-based compression, it further shortens the CoT of a model already trained for brevity. Ablations and behavioral analysis show that DoubtLess reduces repeated checking, with most token savings coming after the correct answer first appears in the CoT. Our code is available at https://github.com/leoluolol/DoubtLess.

articles.title: AesCode: Aesthetic Code Generation with Decoupled Cross-Modal Rewards
articles.content: Generating information-rich visual artifacts such as slides, posters, and dashboards as code is appealing because the outputs are structured, editable, and verifiable. Yet code models cannot see how their choices of layout and color come together on the canvas, often limiting spatial planning and aesthetic quality. Image generators excel at visual design but can misrender requested content, making their outputs unreliable targets for direct reproduction. We therefore introduce AesCode, which generates code grounded in the content prompt while using an image generated from the same prompt as an aesthetic guidance. To do so, AesCode represents the target as a design graph that describes the whole canvas and makes each property attributable. From this graph, we derive complementary cross-modal rewards: deterministic verifiers score properties parsable from code and rendering, while a VLM judge assesses the non-parsable ones with a sample-specific Visual Graph Rubric (VGR) tied to graph elements and relations. We optimize these decoupled rewards through reinforcement learning with per-channel normalization to jointly improve spatial planning, aesthetic quality, and verifiable correctness. To evaluate this setting, we build a benchmark that scores verifiable correctness and visual quality separately, with visual scores highly consistent with human judgments. We find that reference images substantially improve the visual quality of code generated by existing models, and ablations show that AesCode benefits from references both as model input and as a source of visual rewards. Relative to same-scale Qwen3-VL baselines given the same references, AesCode-8B and AesCode-32B improve visual quality by 31.1 and 22.4 percentage points, reaching scores comparable to those of closed-source frontier models such as GPT-5.5 and Claude Opus 4.8.

articles.title: Hybrid Reasoning Agents
articles.content: How can we build an agent that thinks beyond human language, yet still acts through it in the external environment? Modern LLM agents still reason and interact through text, while latent reasoning offers an efficient internal medium but lacks native tool access and reasoning transparency. We bridge these two directions with Hybrid Reasoning Agents (HybridAgents), which dynamically navigate between latent reasoning and text-based interaction throughout a unified generation process. Architecturally, a lightweight HybridLink enables seamless transitions between text and latent modes, while the agent's continuous working memory preserves lossless hybrid context across multiple turns. These designs preserve tool-integrated agentic capabilities while making latent thoughts directly inspectable. Building on this architecture, we further develop dedicated post-training algorithms for hybrid reasoning: HybridSFT stabilizes tool-integrated hybrid generation by teaching the backbone to coordinate with HybridLink, then HybridRL scales reasoning by learning when to think in latent space and when to act through text. We evaluate HybridAgent at 3 model scales across 11 benchmarks covering mathematics, science, medicine, search, and agentic reasoning. Compared with frontier LLM Agents and agentic frameworks spanning both text-based and latent methods, HybridAgent consistently improves performance by 10.4%, while delivering 35.5%-54.7% token reduction, 1.8x-2.6x faster inference, and 2.7x-3.7x cost savings. Code and data are available at https://github.com/togethercomputer/HybridAgent.

articles.title: Visual Tokens on Demand: Visual Budgeting for Scalable and Efficient Multi-Image Reasoning in Multimodal LLMs
articles.content: Multimodal large language models have advanced rapidly, but most remain optimized for single-image inputs. Multi-image reasoning is costly because each image adds many visual tokens, increasing encoding and attention demands. Existing techniques that address the above issue, including visual token pruning, token merging, visual token compression, learned resampling, hierarchical compression, retrieval-augmented visual reasoning, and memory-based architectures, have largely been designed for single-image scenarios, where redundancy is primarily spatial and local. Multi-image reasoning introduces additional challenges: redundancy may occur across images, task-relevant evidence may be sparse or distributed, and aggressive per-image compression can remove details needed for comparison, counting, temporal reasoning, retrieval, or evidence grounding. Moreover, existing token-reduction methods are often either (i) training-free but inference-inefficient, typically relying on accessing attention matrices to get token-importance that may be impractical to access with memory-efficient attention implementations such as FlashAttention, or (ii) training-dependent, requiring the base MLLM to be retrained or adapted to a new compressed-token paradigm. In this work, we study scalable multi-image reasoning and understanding without retraining the base model and without accessing attention matrices at inference time. To this end, we propose mmVB, a lightweight plug-and-play module that assigns query-conditioned per-image token budgets via cross-image context, adding only 1.6M trainable parameters while reducing visual input tokens by 9x. This reduction yields 5x faster time-to-first-token and 7x fewer prefill FLOPs, while maintaining 94.4% of full-resolution accuracy across eight multi-image reasoning benchmarks.

articles.title: PixelMoE: Scaling Pixel-Space Diffusion with LLM-Style Mixture-of-Experts
articles.content: Pixel-space diffusion models provide an appealing alternative to latent-space diffusion models by directly modeling raw images without relying on a learned tokenizer. However, scaling pixel-space models has predominantly followed dense strategies, tightly coupling model capacity with active computation. In this work, we show that standard LLM-style Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) architectures can be effectively transferred to pixel-space diffusion. Building on this finding, we introduce PixelMoE, a pixel-space generative framework that sparsely scales model capacity with standard LLM-style MoE, without diffusion-specific routing mechanisms or auxiliary routing objectives. Specifically, PixelMoE combines standard Token-Choice (TC) routing with fine-grained routed experts for input-adaptive sparse computation, a shared expert for capturing common representations, and a bias-based load-balancing strategy. To complement sparse capacity scaling, PixelMoE further introduces Pixel-Space Hierarchical Flow Matching, which varies spatial resolution along the denoising trajectory from global structure formation to fine-grained detail refinement. At comparable active parameter counts, PixelMoE consistently outperforms its dense counterparts across model scales, demonstrating effective sparse capacity scaling in pixel space. On class-conditional ImageNet-1K, PixelMoE achieves FID scores of 1.47 at 256x256 and 1.53 at 512x512 without representation alignment or perceptual losses, comparing favorably with leading pixel-space and latent-space generative models. Code and models will be released soon.

articles.title: Exact Topological Compliance: Generating Persistence-Equivalent Graphs
articles.content: Persistent homology summarizes the topological evolution of a graph as persistence diagrams (PDs). Generating graphs whose topology matches a target descriptor is increasingly important, yet existing topology-aware generative models rely on soft regularization, producing graphs whose PDs may only be approximately similar. We initiate a principled investigation of the generation problem: produce graphs that realize a target PD exactly. We propose two approaches guided by the implicit local and global constraints a target PD imposes. The local approach builds degree-based PD-equivalent graphs iteratively, and we prove that every output realizes the target PD and that every degree-based PD-equivalent graph is reachable. However, as shown thereafter, local generation necessarily trades off between sample diversity and reaching infeasible states. We therefore recast generation as a global constraint satisfaction problem with a complete encoding solvable by modern constraint programming solvers. This is applicable to any vertex-based permutation equivariant filtration scheme and is minimal under the degree filtration. Experiments on four standard graph generation benchmarks confirm that both methods realize the target PD exactly. Together, our methods provide a principled treatment of strict topology-compliant graph generation. Code is available at https://github.com/Aalto-QuML/ExactCompliance.

articles.title: Interaction Latents as Actions for Contact-Rich Manipulation
articles.content: Contact-rich manipulation requires robots to coordinate not only where to move, but also how contact and force should evolve throughout an interaction. Yet most robot policies represent actions primarily as motion trajectories, using tactile signals as inputs or auxiliary prediction targets without explicitly encoding contact dynamics in the action representation. We propose ILA (Interaction Latents as Actions), which uses decodable interaction latents that jointly capture the evolution of motion, contact, and force application as policy action units, providing a shared representation for action generation, evaluation, and offline improvement. We learn these latents through visually conditioned joint action-tactile reconstruction with a time-conditioned implicit decoder. Using them as flow-matching generation targets supports post-training of pretrained vision-language-action models (VLAs) and world action models (WAMs), as well as training flow-matching policies from scratch. A shared decoder maps generated latents to executable actions. For offline improvement, we learn a tactile-conditioned expert reference model from interaction latents encoded from expert demonstrations. The resulting expert-consistency rewards guide weighted learning from successful rollouts, while observation-compatible expert references guide correction of low-reward predictions from failed rollouts. Across three policy families, ILA improves success rates averaged over four real-world tasks by 21.0-36.5 percentage points relative to tactile-conditioned direct-action baselines. Ablations highlight the benefit of encoding contact evolution in action targets beyond tactile conditioning, while the same latent space supports expert-guided offline improvement. Project website: https://mrsecant.github.io/ILA/.

articles.title: Two Clocks: Why Larger Rollout Batches Learn Slower but Fail on Schedule in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards
articles.content: Reinforcement learning with verifiable rewards (RLVR) relies on costly model-generated responses, motivating larger rollout batches and square-root learning-rate scaling. Reported to approximately preserve progress per sample with one optimizer step per rollout, this rule is less understood in practical multi-step training. We develop a two-clock framework that separates the samples needed to make progress from those consumed before collapse. Under a local quadratic model, the square-root rule preserves first-order drift per sample but not progress: larger batches take fewer, longer updates and lose more to curvature, yielding a learning-rate-dependent critical batch beyond which sample efficiency degrades. A drift-threshold hypothesis predicts a complementary failure clock whose sample count remains approximately invariant along the square-root rule. Controlled GRPO experiments on Qwen2.5-Math-1.5B across a $16\times$ batch range support both predictions. Ratio clipping delays failure, especially for larger batches, but the progress gap persists without it. Widening the clip trades stability for a transient speed gain. The progress gap reappears on another dataset, a general-purpose checkpoint, and a 7B model. Finally, we use the two-clock framework to derive a simple multi-step RLVR schedule: start below the critical batch and switch to a larger batch before failure. Our code is available at: https://github.com/WinstonLiyt/two-clocks-rlvr.

articles.title: ForceWAM: Decoupling Future and Response Learning from Demo and Play Data for Contact-Rich Manipulation
articles.content: Expert demonstrations show how to complete contact-rich tasks, but provide limited coverage of how interaction forces respond to different actions. Task-agnostic play provides broader experience of contact dynamics without specifying task goals. To fully leverage these two types of data, we introduce ForceWAM, a force world action model that decouples knowledge of task-compatible interaction outcomes from knowledge of how local actions change contact. A world model learns from successful demonstrations to jointly predict future video and six-axis force/torque trajectories. Together, these futures describe the expected evolution of motion and contact during the task. A separate inverse dynamics model (IDM) learns from both task and play, mapping current observations and recorded visual-wrench futures to their associated robot actions. Play data thus provide knowledge of force responses for goal-directed execution. At deployment, the IDM reactively translates generated futures into actions, reusing them with fresh wrench feedback between world-model updates. Across real-robot force-regulated sliding, box flipping with and without disturbances, and ring placement, ForceWAM achieves $85$-$95\%$ mean success, surpassing world-modeling and reactive baselines. Our experiments further show that adding task-agnostic play data improves success by $15$-$45$ percentage points, demonstrating its value for learning contact-rich execution. Project page and code are available at https://force-wam.github.io/.

articles.title: MFG: Multi-turn Feedback Guided Molecular Optimization
articles.content: Multi-objective molecular optimization is a critical process in drug discovery that aims to modify a given molecule to simultaneously improve multiple properties while maintaining a similar overall structure. This process often requires iterative modifications guided by computational or experimental feedback. Recent large language model (LLM)-based methods have begun to explore this iterative approach; however, these methods are not explicitly trained to leverage such feedback, while existing approaches primarily focus on single-turn molecular optimization. To address this gap, we introduce Multi-turn Feedback Guided (MFG) molecular optimization, a reinforcement learning framework that trains an LLM to progressively optimize molecules using feedback from previous turns. MFG introduces a feedback vector capturing both property improvements and source molecule similarity, alongside a feedback-aligned reward function that promotes progressive improvement across turns. We apply MFG over $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$, a state-of-the-art LLM model for multi-objective molecular optimization, evaluate $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ on ten multi-objective molecular optimization tasks. The results demonstrate that $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O-MFG}$ achieves the highest average similarity-constrained success rate ($81.50%$), outperforming the base model $\text{GeLLM}^{3}\text{O}$ ($70.81%$).

articles.title: Collaborative Planning for UAV-UGV Teams under Operational Constraints via Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion
articles.content: Collaborative planning under operational constraints is essential for heterogeneous robot teams in large-scale missions. Unmanned Aerial Vehicles (UAVs) provide rapid area coverage but are limited by onboard energy, while Unmanned Ground Vehicles (UGVs) can serve as mobile recharging stations yet are constrained by road-network traversability. Effective collaboration must enforce operational constraints during execution while enabling parallel, coordinated actions. Masked Diffusion Models (MDMs) have shown promise through token unmasking but have two key limitations: entropy-guided scheduling assumes distributional alignment and reliance on differentiable constraints for diffusion-time optimization. We propose Masked Error-bounded Neuro-Symbolic Diffusion (MEND), which formulates collaborative planning as a conditional masked generative process to generate context-aware action sequences for UAV-UGV teams. MEND introduces a neuro-symbolic diffusion paradigm that constrains conditional masked diffusion policies at execution by reweighting the learned action distribution with a logic-induced admissibility indicator, thereby enforcing compliance with operational constraints. MEND introduces an error-bounded inference scheduling at execution that constructs the unmasking schedule by selecting positions with minimal predictive entropy over the constraint-aware action distribution, enhancing collaborative planning optimality under operational constraints. Extensive experimental results in simulation, on real-world maps, and with physical robot teams demonstrate that MEND advances UAV-UGV collaborative planning under operational constraints.

articles.title: Contact Trajectory Prompting: In-Context Transfer of Contact-Rich Behaviors from a Single Demonstration
articles.content: In-context robot learning enables robots to acquire new behaviors from demonstrations without test-time parameter updates. However, visual and kinematic specifications alone may not distinguish contact-rich behaviors that share similar motions but require different interaction intensities or patterns. We propose Contact Trajectory Prompting (CTP), a framework for one-shot transfer of contact-rich manipulation behaviors. CTP encodes motion and contact information from a single demonstration into an ordered contact trajectory prompt that captures their temporal evolution and specifies the desired physical interaction behavior. During execution, the policy uses online sensory feedback to retrieve interaction-relevant information from the prompt, conditioning closed-loop action generation on the demonstrated contact behavior. Across real-world wiping, rotation, and insertion tasks on objects excluded from training, CTP achieves 78.7% overall success, outperforming the strongest evaluated baseline by 13.0 percentage points. Changing only the reference demonstration enables CTP to follow contact specifications for both intensity and direction, including an intermediate wiping force level and clockwise or counterclockwise cap rotation. These results demonstrate that contact trajectories serve as effective behavioral specifications, extending in-context robot learning beyond motion imitation to physical interaction transfer. articles.title: WorldRecon: Generative Multi-View Mesh Reconstruction for Large-Scale 3D World
articles.content: Reconstructing complete, high-quality meshes of large-scale scenes from unposed multi-view images requires faithful geometric grounding while plausibly completing surfaces that are unobserved or only sparsely captured. We present WorldRecon, a generative multi-view reconstruction framework for recovering complete, large-scale 3D scene meshes from unposed RGB images. WorldRecon uses a coarse, noisy global point cloud and camera poses estimated from the input images by a reconstruction model as a global scaffold for whole-scene generation and partitions it into overlapping spatial blocks. To robustly leverage these imperfect geometric priors, we equip the native 3D generative model TRELLIS.2 with a dedicated reconstruction-based conditioning architecture that generates each block from its local point-cloud crop and block-relevant image observations, producing sparse structure, detailed geometry, and PBR materials. To maintain scene-level coherence, we introduce neighbour-aware latent inpainting and a causal world-generation procedure that propagates structural, geometric, and material context across overlapping blocks. Together, these designs scale multi-view generative reconstruction to large-scale scenes, yielding coherent, unified meshes. Extensive experiments demonstrate that WorldRecon achieves state-of-the-art reconstruction performance, reducing Chamfer distance by 14.9% and 43.1% while improving F-score by 17.3% and 12.0% over the strongest baselines on synthetic and real-world indoor scenes, respectively, thereby demonstrating faithful and complete generative reconstruction as well as strong sim-to-real generalization. articles.title: The Last Remote Sensing Model Built by Humans? Casting Any Earth Observation Task as Recursive Self-Improvement
articles.content: Earth observation (EO) models are still built by hand. For each new task, experts design a training recipe and tune it against a benchmark. We show that this loop can be handed to an agent. Any verifiable task can be cast as a harness and a verifier, where the harness defines what the agent may use and the verifier defines what counts as success. Every EO task can be made verifiable, through labeled benchmarks, independent sensors, physical models or the repeated observation of the same place. Given only these two components, a general-purpose coding agent builds the EO model and improves it recursively on its own outputs. Settings long treated as separate research problems, from learning with a handful of labels to adapting across domains, become choices of harness and verifier. On four EO benchmarks spanning optical, SAR and multispectral time-series imagery, agent-built models surpass the state of the art and keep most of that accuracy from about 1% of the training labels. This establishes a new paradigm for EO, in which people design harnesses and verifiers and agents build the models, so EO models improve as agents do.

articles.title: RepProbe: Can Video Language Models Count Repeated Actions? A Diagnostic Benchmark
articles.content: Repetition counting requires identifying and enumerating action cycles over time. While state-of-the-art video language models describe actions fluently, they fail to reliably count how many times an action repeats. To investigate this limitation, we introduce RepProbe, a benchmark of 42K real and synthetic video clips containing exactly k in [1, 20] complete repetitions, with controls for clip position, temporal coverage, and duration. These controls allow us to study the counting failure directly and locate where in the model it arises. Counting accuracy collapses at high counts across the video language models we evaluate, and controlled experiments show this collapse is not explained by frame sampling alone. We compare model outputs with linear probes trained on the final-layer representations used to generate those outputs. We find a consistent representation-to-output dissociation: substantial count information remains linearly decodable even when models fail to report the correct count. Further analysis shows this failure arises primarily at the output stage, where answers concentrate on a small set of preferred numbers rather than the available count information. The dissociation holds on both real and synthetic videos and is not explained by clip duration, position, or scene content. These results indicate that models encode repetition structure but do not reliably report it in their outputs. Project page: https://arenaa.github.io/RepProbe-webpage/

articles.title: LIBERO-RIG: A Hardware-Setup Robustness Benchmark for Vision-Language-Action Models
articles.content: Robot policies are expected to generalize across deployment environments, including variations in the robot itself: cameras are bumped and remounted, calibrations drift, controllers run at different rates, and end-effector pads wear down. We present LIBERO-RIG, a benchmark that perturbs only the robot's hardware and setup while holding every LIBERO task fixed. The benchmark spans eleven perturbation axes, including camera mounting and optics, camera-to-arm calibration, actuation gain, control rate, proprioceptive noise, base pose, table height, and gripper pads. Each axis has five severity levels, yielding 210 conditions across the four LIBERO suites. We evaluate nine recent vision-language-action models using 500 episodes per condition and substantiate each finding with rigorous statistical tests. Pooled success falls from 0.932 to 0.767 at the middle severity and 0.509 at the highest severity. Performance degradation varies substantially across perturbation axes and action interfaces, and training on visual perturbations does not mitigate faults that leave camera images unchanged. We release the benchmark together with manifests specifying the fixed perturbation parameters for each episode.

articles.title: Who Improves the Robot? Toward Physical Recursive Self-Improvement
articles.content: Robots are increasingly autonomous in task execution, yet their improvement remains largely human-driven. This study investigates Physical Recursive Self-Improvement (Physical RSI), in which physical experience guides lasting updates to both a robot's capabilities and its improvement procedure, making subsequent improvement more effective across tasks. Physical RSI faces challenges from noisy observations, continuous dynamics, costly trials, and irreversible consequences. We present an L0-L5 framework that differentiates capability-level from meta-level updates and within-task from across-task gains, reserving L5 for independently verified recursive gain. We study existing methods around harness adaptation and model training, alongside safety and control mechanisms that govern execution and successive updates. Our analysis reveals that, despite substantial progress in self-improvement, the surveyed literature does not yet demonstrate Physical RSI as defined by our framework. We identify research priorities in reliable feedback, causal attribution, safety preservation, and benchmarking, outlining a path toward robots that autonomously improve how they learn while ensuring safety. The GitHub repository for Physical RSI is available at https://github.com/SAIL-Research-Lab/Physical-RSI.

articles.title: Fast Rates for Offline Q-Learning with KL Regularization
articles.content: This paper investigates offline Q-learning for finite-horizon Markov decision processes with Kullback-Leibler (KL) regularization. Recent studies have shown that KL regularization can yield fast rates in offline decision-making problems. However, it remains unclear whether Q-learning, which adopts incremental stochastic approximation updates, can achieve such fast rates in the offline setting. We first propose KL-regularized Q-Learning (KLQ), a simple variant of classical Q-learning. By exploiting KL regularization, we prove that KLQ achieves a sample complexity of $\widetilde{O}(1/ε)$ without explicit pessimism. This guarantee, however, has an exponential dependence on the KL regularization parameter and the horizon. To address this limitation, we further propose KL-regularized Pessimistic Q-Learning (KLPQ), which incorporates pessimism into KLQ. We prove that KLPQ retains the same \(\widetilde O(1/ε)\) rate while removing the explicit exponential dependence, thereby further improving the sample complexity. To the best of our knowledge, these results establish the first fast-rate guarantees for offline Q-learning in tabular finite-horizon KL-regularized MDPs.

articles.title: Scaling Online Optimal Transport Minibatches for Flow Matching
articles.content: A central challenge in scaling flow models is maintaining stability in training and integration. In flow matching, this stability depends critically on how source samples are paired with data. Independent random pairing introduces substantial stochasticity, motivating minibatch optimal transport (OT) to construct online source-target couplings that reduce this randomness (Tong et al., 2024). However, as applications extend to larger and higher-dimensional datasets, small minibatches can limit these benefits, while scaling the coupling to substantially larger minibatches at every iteration is computationally prohibitive. Moreover, how OT coupling affects the full stochastic gradient and integration remains theoretically unresolved. In this work, we develop a scalable online entropic OT approximation that enables substantially larger source-target couplings while preserving the benefits of OT. We close the theoretical gap for both unregularized and entropic OT by proving strict reductions in full stochastic-gradient variance and integration error relative to independent pairing, and further characterize how these improvements strengthen as the online coupling minibatch grows. Experiments on single-cell gene interpolation-flow and image-flow training validate these predictions, showing that larger online couplings consistently improve training stability and final generation performance.
